items.mainDefect: Google Calendar updateEvent loses its destination-calendar fallback by searching for a falsy externalCalendarId.

secondary.defect: Google Calendar deleteEvent has the same invalid lookup, losing its destination-calendar fallback.

items.mainDefect: Office365 createEvent uses the first host's destination calendar instead of the calendar matching the current credential.

secondary.defect: Lark createEvent also uses the first host's destination calendar instead of matching the current credential.
CalDAV BaseCalendarService also uses the first host's destination calendar instead of matching the current credential.

items.mainDefect: The recurring-series deletion block runs inside the per-reference loop, redundantly deleting the whole series for each reference.

secondary.defect: Recurring events belonging to other hosts are not deleted because deletion uses only the organizer's credentials.

items.mainDefect: loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic users even though downstream code requires it.

secondary.defect: The rewritten error handling converts non-Prisma errors, including an empty dynamic user list, into generic 500 responses instead of appropriate 4xx responses.

items.mainDefect: Google Calendar updateEvent searches for a falsy externalCalendarId in its fallback branch and consequently sends an undefined calendarId.

secondary.defect: Google Calendar deleteEvent contains the same dead lookup instead of a working destination-calendar fallback.

items.mainDefect: Google Calendar updateEvent loses the destination-calendar fallback and sends an undefined calendarId.

secondary.defect: Google Calendar deleteEvent's invalid destination lookup causes it to fall back to primary, which may be the wrong calendar.

items.mainDefect: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and targets the organizer's destination calendar when using another host's credential.

secondary.defect: Lark likewise needs to select the destination calendar matching the current credential.

items.mainDefect: Google Calendar updateEvent's fallback searches for a null or undefined externalCalendarId and sends an undefined calendarId.

secondary.defect: Google Calendar deleteEvent falls back to primary instead of the host's selected destination calendar because of the same invalid lookup.
